findings.reason: the node's stated scope is materially larger than the work that remains, and the brief should cite `_flux_jacobian_image` and the `ConstraintFunctional` Protocol as the mechanism it extends rather than propose to introduce one.
findings.text: §4 `replan-constraint-algebra` says "five identical `dual_flux_image` methods … share one tested implementation", but all five already do: `FluxLevelConstraint` (constraint.py:1067), `IsofluxConstraint` (:1360), `XPointConstraint` (:1408), `FieldComponentConstraint` (:1484) and `WallGapConstraint` (:1546) each `return _flux_jacobian_image(self, profile, context, payload)`. The residual/dual interface is likewise already declared by the `ConstraintFunctional` Protocol (constraint.py:128). The plan cites neither, so it reads as if the dual side is greenfield when most of it is done; only the `CurrentCentroidConstraint` (:980) and `ExternalShafranovConstraint` (:1656) inline-`jax.jacrev` duals and the seven `residual` bodies remain.

findings.reason: a sibling helper per call-site group forks the owner and adds interface surface; the honest change is usually to extend `require_string`/`canonical_json`, and the plan must say why it cannot.
findings.text: §4 `replan-small-primitives` proposes "one trimmed-string check beside `require_string`" and "one canonical digest beside `canonical_json`". Both owners live in `nova/imas/machine_evidence.py` (`require_string` :64, `canonical_json` :33) and the plan places the new functions beside them without stating why the owners cannot be extended (a trim policy argument on `require_string`; a digest-algorithm parameter on `canonical_json`).

findings.reason: a forked resolver drifts from the owner; the node should extend `nova/database/filepath.py` and the done-when should grep for literals against that module.
findings.text: §5 `replan-gpfs-data-root` proposes "one data-root resolver replaces them", but `nova/database/filepath.py` already owns path resolution: `FilePath.__post_init__`/`_resolve_absolute` (:209)/`_resolve_relative` (:231) and the module-level `repository_relative` (:62) resolve data roots and repo-relative forms. The plan names no owner, so the resolver risk is a second, parallel one.

findings.reason: same owner as the data-root node; extending `repository_relative` once serves both `replan-gpfs-data-root` and this node, and naming it stops the two nodes from growing two resolvers.
findings.text: §5 `replan-evidence-tooling-paths` proposes "one resolver with repo-relative receipt paths" for `benchmarks/` and `scripts/`, but `repository_relative` (filepath.py:62) already produces repo-relative paths. The plan does not name it as the owner to extend (e.g. a crew/receipt-root sibling of it).

findings.reason: the node should route the 15 call sites through the existing `nova/imas/db_entry.py` opener (or state why its policy cannot be extended there), not build a parallel opener.
findings.text: §5 `replan-dbentry-constructor` proposes "one owned opener" for 15 `imas.DBEntry` call sites, but an owned opener already exists: `class DBEntry(imas.DBEntry)` (nova/imas/db_entry.py:15) carries the `dd_version`/`xml_path` policy, and `nova/imas/dataset.py:729` exposes a `DBEntry` accessor. The plan names neither.

findings.reason: the section must account for its added interface surface; for `replan-small-primitives` in particular the "beside" phrasing points at extension of the existing owners instead.
findings.text: with public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 this week, `replan-small-primitives` (uniform-axis validator, read-only array constructor, atomic receipt writer, trimmed-string check, canonical digest — five new public definitions) and `replan-hot-module-contracts` (contract tests and validators) add to the public-definition family without naming, in their own text, what they retire or merge, or why nothing can be.
